name: Bone Rush

gist.Vacarn, the Dark Goblin Necromancer: Skeletons he raises from the discard pile with Necromancy keep their effects and may use them at once. Low health.
gist.Cute Nerd Magenta: Discards a card to send any card from the deck to the discard pile, where the Skeletons are wanted.
gist.Alice, the Puppeteer Girl: Once per turn hits one of your targets, harder for every creature that has stayed on her board.
gist.Rain of Arrows: Hits your whole side, harder for every creature she controls.
gist.Necromancy: Ability: each turn summons a creature from the discard pile as a free action.
gist.Skeleton Necromancer: Discards a card to raise another Skeleton.
gist.Skeleton Demon: Whenever you draw or search cards with your own effects, it hits a target for each card.
gist.Hammer Skeleton: Each turn smashes a spell attached to a hero, or an Area.
gist.Skeleton Skull Bat: Makes you discard a card every turn.
gist.Skeleton Death Knight: Stops one of your heroes from acting until the end of your next turn.
gist.Skeleton Bard: Lets another Skeleton use its effect twice.
gist.Loyal Bone Dog: Discarded from hand to revive a Skeleton that just died.
gist.Glass of Marbles: Draws two when it is discarded.
gist.Divine Gift of Fire: Once per game: sets your whole side on fire for good.

plan: Skeletons are small, die easily and do not stay dead. Each has one useful trick per turn (a heavy shot, a discard, a smashed attachment, a locked hero), and Isolde keeps the right ones on the board by raising them with Necromancy every turn; raised by Vacarn they act immediately. Magenta stocks the discard pile, the Bard doubles the best effect, and the row itself is a weapon: Alice and Rain of Arrows both count her creatures. The army is as fragile as it looks and has to be rebuilt after every sweep; Vacarn, the hero who makes it fast, is the frailest thing on her side.

looks.early: A Town Guard, a Skeleton Mage, Skeletons going into the discard pile on purpose.
looks.mid: Five Skeletons each doing one thing a turn, another rising at the start of each of her turns, Alice counting.
looks.late: A board rebuilt for the third time, a Hammer Skeleton eyeing your Storm, Rain of Arrows in hand.

opening.tell: Her Skeletons have just been summoned from hand and cannot use their effects until next turn.
opening.why: A Skeleton that dies before its first turn has done nothing, and a Hammer Skeleton left alive will smash Gathering Storm the moment it is attached.

midgame.tell: Vacarn raises a Skeleton every turn and that Skeleton acts immediately; a Skeleton Demon watches your draws.
midgame.why: Sweeps only buy a turn while Vacarn stands; he has the least health on her side, and without him raised Skeletons arrive blank. A setup turn full of draws is paid for through the Demon.

crisis.tell: Her board is five Skeletons wide and she is holding Rain of Arrows.
crisis.why: Alice and Rain of Arrows both scale with that row: a sweep before her turn makes both nearly harmless, and racing three heroes while five Skeletons act loses.

endgame.tell: Her discard pile is thin and few Skeletons are left to raise.
endgame.why: With the recursion running dry, her heroes cannot stop the Storm on their own.

opening.board: Isolde summons a Skeleton Mage and a Hammer Skeleton; neither can act yet.
